title: 'A blowout': US added 165,000 jobs in October, trouncing expectations
summary:
The US added 165,000 jobs in October, blowing past economists' expectations, as the labor market showed strength despite the Federal Reserve's recent rate hikes.
September's underwhelming jobs report of 29,000 additions was also revised upward to a gain of 60,000 jobs.
Employers added jobs in a number of sectors of the economy.
Healthcare, long a strong spot for job growth, added a higher-than-average 42,000 positions.
Other job market measures released earlier this week telegraphed steady hiring — though not to the extent of Friday's report blowout number.

(AP Photo/LM Otero)WASHINGTON -- Fewer Americans applied for unemployment benefits last week as layoffs remain scarce and most workers enjoy job security.
The Labor Department reported Thursday that 189,000 people sought jobless aid last week, the fewest since mid-July and down from 195,000 the week before.

A jobs report on Friday showed hiring accelerated in October, providing the first major snapshot of the economy since the midterms as the stock market seesaws in response to the election results.
Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, an increase from 60,000 jobs added a month earlier, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed.
Hiring in October came in well above an average of 48,000 jobs added each month over the previous 12 months, the BLS said.

title: Federal Reserve rate hike bets strengthen as US jobs growth beats estimates
summary:
SynopsisStronger than expected US jobs growth has revived expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate hike, with employers adding 165,000 jobs in October against estimates of 65,000.
The unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, while markets raised the probability of a quarter point hike to 85% and brought forward expectations of another increase.
